NWS Seattle at 2:14 AM PDT: A ridge offshore in the Pacific is beginning to amplify a bit in between two upper level lows/troughs, one over the northern Great Plains/Upper Midwest, and the other over the north Pacific. Down at the surface, it's the opposite effect as MSLP has a thermally induced surface trough along the coast developing as conditions warm under the ridge. The combination of the two will lead to warmer temperatures, and drier conditions as the flow will turn offshore at times. This offshore flow is also expected to bring in smoke from fires in eastern WA over the next couple days. Soundings favor some of the smoke to mix down to the surface as temperatures warm at the surface, breaking the shallow inversion just aloft. For the most up to date smoke and air quality information in your area, please visit airnow.gov or your local air quality agency. Besides smoke, heat will be the other factor to be aware of as the ridge/thermal trough set up in the area. While smoke may play a factor in holding temperatures during the day a few degrees cooler, high temperatures in the upper 80s/low to mid 90s in the interior, with lows in the upper 50s to low 60s will likely lead to a 2-3 day stretch of widespread Moderate (Orange) HeatRisk across much of the interior. There is a 20-30% chance of south Puget Sound urban areas seeing Major (Red) HeatRisk Wednesday and Thursday. If planning to spend time outdoors next couple days, consider taking frequent breaks indoors in a cooledbuilding as much as possible.
